text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"TO BE HARDENED UPTO 32-35 HRC."}],"comment":"The heat treatment specifies a hardness of 32-35 HRC but does not state the manufacturing stage at which it applies (e.g., before or after machining, before plating). This matters because hardening after final machining can distort tight-tolerance features like D4 and D5, and hardening before plating affects process sequencing. The designer should add the stage to the heat treatment note (for example, 'HARDEN TO 32-35 HRC PRIOR TO FINAL MACHINING AND PLATING').","recommended_correction":"Update the heat treatment field or note N11 to specify the manufacturing stage at which the 32-35 HRC hardness is to be achieved."},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D4","page":1,"quote":"⌀12 H7"},{"kind":"title_block","ref":"surface_treatment","page":1,"quote":"I.Z.B.P. (TRIVALENT)"}],"comment":"Dimension D4 carries an ISO fit callout (H7) on a part that receives I.Z.B.P. (trivalent zinc) plating, yet no allowance for plating thickness is indicated. This matters because the plating will build up inside the hole, potentially making the finished bore undersize and preventing the intended mating fit. The designer should either adjust the pre-plate tolerance to account for the coating thickness or add a note specifying reaming/broaching after plating.","recommended_correction":"Add a plating-thickness allowance to the ⌀12 H7 dimension or specify that the hole is to be finished to size after surface treatment."}]}
